cards.text: The temple's done, the ark is in its place, and a cloud fills the house with the glory of the LORD. The priests can't even stand there to minister, and friend, I sat out of work for YEARS in a junk drawer with nowhere near that good an excuse. Then Solomon, king of Israel and David's son, speaks: “The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.”

cards.question: True or false: Solomon tells the LORD he has built Him a house to dwell in forever.

cards.text: Then the king turns around to face the whole assembly of Israel standing there. And he blesses them all.

cards.question: Solomon blesses the LORD for doing with His own hand what He spoke with His mouth. Who did God make that promise to?

cards.text: Solomon repeats what the LORD said back then. Since the day He brought His people out of Egypt, He hadn't chosen a city from any tribe to build a house for His Name, or anyone to rule over His people.

cards.question: But now, the LORD says, He has chosen ___ for His Name to be there, and ___ to be over His people Israel.

cards.text: Here's the backstory, friend. Building a house for the Name of the LORD was in David's heart first.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell David about having that house in his heart?

answers.text: He did well to have it in his heart
He should have asked a prophet first
He was reaching too high for a king

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells David that he is the one who will build the house.

cards.text: Nope, it's David's own son, and now Solomon sits on his father's throne with the house built, just as the LORD promised. God says it, God does it, and meanwhile I've been promising my ovens a deep clean since the day I got here.

cards.question: Solomon says he has placed something inside the house he built. What is it?

answers.text: The ark holding the LORD's covenant
The sword that belonged to Goliath

cards.text: Then Solomon stands before the altar of the LORD, in front of the whole assembly of Israel. He's had a bronze platform made, five cubits long, five wide and three high, and set in the middle of the courtyard.

cards.question: Solomon steps up onto that bronze platform in front of the whole assembly. What does he do up there?

answers.text: Kneels and spreads his hands toward heaven
Reads the law of Moses out loud
Holds up the tablets for all to see

cards.text: Friend, I have stood on a base my WHOLE renewed life, and it never once crossed my mind to kneel on it. Solomon's out here teaching ME things.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon begins his prayer by telling the LORD there are other gods just like Him in heaven.

cards.text: Solomon says God kept His promise to David this very day. Now he asks God to keep another one: David will never fail to have a man to sit on the throne of Israel.

cards.question: That throne promise comes with an if. David's descendants must guard their way to walk in God's ___, as David did.

cards.text: Solomon asks God to confirm what He promised David. Then he stops and asks the big one: will God really dwell with people on earth?

cards.question: Solomon wonders if God will really dwell with people on earth. What does he say can't contain God?

cards.text: The highest heavens can't contain God, much less this temple, and Solomon knows it. Still, he asks the LORD to hear his prayer and to keep His eyes open toward this temple, the place where God said He would put His Name.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon asks for God's eyes to be open toward the temple day and night.

cards.text: And it's not just Solomon's prayers. He asks God to hear His people Israel too, whenever they pray toward this place.

cards.question: When Israel prays toward the temple, where does Solomon ask God to hear them from?

answers.text: From the top of Mount Zion

cards.question: Solomon asks God to hear from heaven, His dwelling place, and then to ___ His people.

cards.text: Now Solomon gets specific, one case at a time. First: a man sins against his neighbor and has to come take an oath before the altar in this temple.

cards.question: When that man takes his oath before the altar, what does Solomon ask God to do?

answers.text: Judge the wicked and the righteous
Let the priests settle the matter
Let the king decide the matter

cards.text: Next: Israel is defeated by an enemy because they've sinned against God. Then they turn back, confess His name, and pray in this temple.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon asks God to forgive them and bring them back to the land He gave them and their fathers.

cards.text: Next: the skies are shut and there's no rain, because the people have sinned. Then they pray toward this place and turn from their sins.

cards.question: Solomon asks God to forgive them, teach them the good way to walk, and send ___ on the land.

cards.text: Then Solomon names the hard times: famine, plague, blight, mildew, locusts, grasshoppers, enemies besieging their cities, whatever sickness comes. He is covering EVERY base, friend, like somebody reading the fine print on a warranty card out loud.

cards.question: Each person spreads out his hands toward this temple. Solomon asks God to repay each man by his ways, because only God knows the ___ of men.

cards.text: Then Solomon prays for someone outside Israel. It's a foreigner from a distant land who comes because of God's great name and mighty hand.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon asks God to hear the prayers of Israel only, and not the foreigner's.
Why does Solomon want God to answer the foreigner's prayer?

answers.text: So all peoples will know His name and fear Him
So the foreigner will bring the temple rich gifts
So Israel's enemies will be put to shame

cards.question: True or false: When Israel goes to war and prays toward the city and the temple, Solomon asks God to uphold their cause.

cards.text: Next: the people sin against God, and Solomon says it straight: there is no one who does not sin. Not the king, not the priests, and DEFINITELY not the stamper who once stamped a whole batch upside down.

cards.question: Solomon pictures God angry with His people and handing them over to an enemy. What does that enemy do?

answers.text: Takes them captive to a land far or near
Burns every one of their fields
Makes them pay tribute every year

cards.text: Then, in the land of their captors, they come to their senses. They confess they've sinned and done wrong, and they return to God with all their heart and soul.

cards.question: Far away in that enemy land, which way does Solomon say they will pray?

answers.text: Toward their land and the temple
Toward Mount Sinai in the desert
Toward the banks of the Jordan

cards.text: Solomon asks God to hear them from heaven, uphold their cause and forgive His people. Then once more, he asks for God's eyes to be open and His ears attentive to the prayer offered in this place.

cards.question: Solomon calls on the LORD God to arise and enter His ___ place, along with the ark of His might.
Solomon ends by asking God not to reject His anointed one. Whose servant does he ask God to remember His loving devotion to?

cards.text: That's the end of Solomon's prayer. But hold on to your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done yet.
